body:
Alright, I have tested this too (on v4.5.1.stable.official [f62fdbde1]) and can reproduce it. 

<details>
<summary>System Information</summary>
Godot v4.5.1.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7242) - AMD Ryzen 5 3600X 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 31.93 GiB memory
</details>

Some notes to the issue description itself:
The steps to reproduce are missing a few details, one needs to set the camera to "Access as unique name" so the "%" notation works. If you just drop in the camera (default location (0,0,0)) and try to unproject the point (0,0,0) you will get errors (because that point is the extreme point where every pixel meets).
Also having the output constantly be spammed every frame makes it hard to debug, so I modified the script to only print the values when they change.

<details>
<summary>Extended debug script</summary>

```
@tool
extends Node

var projectionMatrix : Projection = Projection.IDENTITY
var unprojectedPoint : Vector2 = Vector2()
var viewportSize : Rect2 = Rect2()

func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
	var newProjectionMatrix = %Camera3D.get_camera_projection()
	if not newProjectionMatrix.w.is_equal_approx(projectionMatrix.w) or\
	not newProjectionMatrix.x.is_equal_approx(projectionMatrix.x) or\
	not newProjectionMatrix.y.is_equal_approx(projectionMatrix.y) or\
	not newProjectionMatrix.z.is_equal_approx(projectionMatrix.z):
		if (Engine.is_editor_hint()):
			print("Projection Matrix in editor:")
		else:
			print("Projection Matrix in running game:")
		projectionMatrix = newProjectionMatrix
		print(projectionMatrix)
		print()
	
	var newViewport : Viewport = %Camera3D.get_viewport()
	var newViewportSize = newViewport.get_visible_rect()
	
	if not newViewportSize.is_equal_approx(viewportSize):
		if (Engine.is_editor_hint()):
			print("Viewport rect in editor:")
		else:
			print("Viewport rect in running game:")
		viewportSize = newViewportSize
		print(viewportSize)
		print()
	
	var newUnprojectedPoint = %Camera3D.unproject_position(Vector3(0, 0, -1))
	if not newUnprojectedPoint.is_equal_approx(unprojectedPoint):
		if (Engine.is_editor_hint()):
			print("Unproject in editor:")
		else:
			print("Unproject in running game:")
		unprojectedPoint = newUnprojectedPoint
		print(unprojectedPoint)
		print()
```

</details>

Now to the actual thing I wanted to say: 
I changed the project to also use a square aspect ratio (by making the project setting "Viewport Height" the same as the "Viewport Width") and then the projection matrices match in editor and game (because they are both square) but the unprojected point is still wrong, because the cameras project onto different viewports. 
So I also added code to the script that gets the current viewport and you can clearly see that the camera, in the editor, is using a viewport that has size 2x2 (the smallest valid viewport size AFAIK). 
I assume that is either because it's not initialized, or it's deliberately done this way, because usually you don't need the render result of a camera in the editor anyway (and I assume the little previews are done with a separate camera object somehow, not sure, I don't know engine details).

If you put the camera below a SubViewport node, then unproject position will always yield the same result. In editor and in game. Since the viewport both use is the one in the scene tree defined by you, and you can change the size of that viewport as you wish.
